tasks.title: Add fuzzy search and faceted filtering to Store
tasks.prompt: Implement advanced search capabilities in Store class with fuzzy matching, faceted filtering, and search highlighting. Add search_fuzzy() method supporting Levenshtein distance matching for text queries, search_faceted() for multi-dimensional filtering with aggregation results, and get_search_highlights() for snippet generation with matched terms highlighted. Support search parameters: fuzzy_threshold (0-1), facet_fields (list of metadata keys), aggregation_functions (count, unique, range), highlight_format (html, markdown, plain), max_results, offset for pagination. Return SearchResult objects containing matched units, relevance scores, facet aggregations, and highlighted snippets. Include query explanation for debugging.
tasks.rationale: Advanced search is essential for large knowledge graphs. Fuzzy matching handles typos and variations, faceted search enables exploratory filtering, and highlighting improves UX. These features are standard in modern search systems (Elasticsearch, Solr) and significantly improve discoverability.
acceptanceCriteria: search_fuzzy() matches text with configurable Levenshtein distance
search_faceted() returns aggregated facet counts and filtered results
get_search_highlights() generates snippets with highlighted matches
Supports pagination with offset and max_results
Returns relevance scores for ranking
Query explanation available for debugging
Performance acceptable for 10k+ unit graphs
Tests cover fuzzy threshold variations and facet combinations

tasks.title: Add graph versioning with history tracking and rollback
tasks.prompt: Implement version control for the graph Store with commit-style snapshots, history tracking, and rollback capabilities. Add commit_snapshot(message, author, metadata) to save current graph state with metadata, get_history(limit, offset, author_filter) to retrieve commit history, rollback_to_version(version_id) to restore graph to previous state, diff_versions(v1, v2) to compare two snapshots, and branch_graph(branch_name) to create named branches for experimentation. Store snapshots efficiently using delta compression for large graphs. Support tags for important versions and merge operations for combining branches. Include version metadata: timestamp, author, message, parent_version_id, affected_units_count.
tasks.rationale: Version control is critical for knowledge graphs that evolve over time. Users need to experiment safely, track changes, understand how the graph developed, and recover from mistakes. This mirrors Git's value for code—essential for production systems and collaborative workflows.
acceptanceCriteria: commit_snapshot() creates recoverable snapshots with metadata
get_history() returns chronological commit history
rollback_to_version() restores graph to previous state
diff_versions() shows added/removed/modified units and edges
branch_graph() creates independent experimental branches
Delta compression keeps storage overhead under 20% for typical graphs
Supports tags for marking important versions
Tests cover branching, merging, and rollback scenarios

tasks.title: Add real-time collaboration with conflict resolution
tasks.prompt: Implement real-time multi-user collaboration for the graph Store with operational transformation (OT) or CRDT-based conflict resolution. Add register_client(client_id, metadata) to join collaborative session, broadcast_operation(op_type, data) to propagate changes, receive_operations(client_id) to fetch remote changes, resolve_conflicts(operations) to handle concurrent edits using OT or CRDT algorithms, and get_active_clients() to list connected users. Support operation types: add_unit, remove_unit, update_unit, add_edge, remove_edge. Include presence awareness showing who's viewing/editing which parts of the graph. Emit events for remote changes to enable real-time UI updates.
tasks.rationale: Collaborative knowledge building is powerful but requires conflict resolution. Multiple users editing the same graph concurrently creates race conditions and merge conflicts. OT/CRDT algorithms solve this, enabling Google Docs-style real-time collaboration for knowledge graphs.
acceptanceCriteria: Multiple clients can edit graph concurrently without data loss
Conflicts automatically resolved using OT or CRDT
broadcast_operation() propagates changes to all clients
receive_operations() fetches and applies remote changes
Presence awareness shows active users and their focus
Operations causally ordered for consistency
Handles network partitions gracefully
Tests cover concurrent edits and conflict scenarios

tasks.title: Add browser extension for web content clipping
tasks.prompt: Create browser extension (Chrome/Firefox/Safari) for clipping web content into the graph. Extension features: 1) Highlight text on any webpage and add as unit with automatic metadata (URL, title, author, timestamp, selection context), 2) Clip entire articles with reader mode extraction (main content, images, metadata), 3) Create edges between clipped units directly in browser, 4) Search existing graph and link new clips to related units, 5) Offline queue for when graph server is unreachable. UI: sidebar panel for search and recent clips, context menu for quick clipping, popup for settings and sync status. Communicate with graph API via REST/GraphQL. Support custom templates for different site types (Twitter, Reddit, GitHub, Medium).
tasks.rationale: Web browsing generates massive amounts of valuable information that's currently siloed in browser bookmarks or lost. A clipping extension makes knowledge capture frictionless at the point of discovery, dramatically increasing graph utility. This is how tools like Notion, Obsidian, and Roam grow user engagement.
acceptanceCriteria: Text selection creates unit with webpage metadata
Article clipping extracts main content using reader mode
Sidebar shows existing units and search results
Context menu provides quick clip actions
Offline queue syncs when connection restored
Custom templates for Twitter, Reddit, GitHub, Medium
Works on Chrome, Firefox, and Safari
Extension settings persist across sessions

tasks.title: Add email newsletter adapter supporting Substack and Buttondown
tasks.prompt: Implement newsletter import adapter supporting Substack and Buttondown APIs. For each platform: authenticate via API key, fetch all newsletters user is subscribed to, import individual posts as units with metadata (title, author, publication, publish_date, content, tags, subscriber_count, like_count), create edges between posts and publications, handle embedded images and links, respect rate limits. Support incremental sync for new posts only. Map newsletter-specific metadata: author_bio, publication_description, category, is_paid, archive_url. Handle HTML content conversion to clean text/markdown. Provide CLI commands: graph import newsletter --platform substack --api-key KEY and graph import newsletter --platform buttondown --token TOKEN.
tasks.rationale: Email newsletters are a major source of curated knowledge (especially technical newsletters, industry insights, research summaries). Substack and Buttondown are the leading platforms. Importing newsletters makes this valuable content searchable, linkable, and integrable with other knowledge sources.
acceptanceCriteria: Substack adapter fetches all subscribed newsletters and posts
Buttondown adapter imports newsletters via API
Units include full content and metadata
Edges connect posts to publications
Incremental sync fetches only new posts
HTML content cleaned to markdown
Rate limiting respected
CLI commands work for both platforms

tasks.title: Add sensor data adapter for IoT time-series ingestion
tasks.prompt: Implement adapter for ingesting IoT sensor data streams in common time-series formats: InfluxDB line protocol, Prometheus metrics, MQTT messages, and CSV time-series. Parse sensor readings into units with metadata: sensor_id, sensor_type, timestamp, value, unit_of_measurement, location, device_id. Create temporal edges between consecutive readings from same sensor. Support aggregation: downsample high-frequency data (e.g., 1-second readings to 1-minute averages) to prevent graph bloat. Handle multiple value types: numeric, boolean, string, JSON. Support batch ingestion from files and streaming ingestion from MQTT brokers or HTTP endpoints. Include data quality checks: detect out-of-range values, gaps, duplicates.
tasks.rationale: IoT and sensor data is increasingly important for personal tracking (smart homes, wearables, environmental monitoring) and industrial applications. Time-series data in knowledge graphs enables correlation analysis (e.g., 'how does room temperature correlate with my productivity?'). Unique challenge is handling high-volume streaming data.
acceptanceCriteria: Parses InfluxDB line protocol, Prometheus, MQTT, CSV formats
Units include sensor metadata and readings
Temporal edges connect consecutive readings
Downsampling reduces high-frequency data
Streaming ingestion from MQTT brokers works
Data quality checks flag anomalies
Supports multiple value types
Batch and streaming modes both functional

tasks.title: Add interactive graph visualization export to Cytoscape.js
tasks.prompt: Implement export adapter generating interactive web-based graph visualizations using Cytoscape.js library. Export produces standalone HTML file with embedded graph data and interactive controls: pan, zoom, node selection, edge filtering, layout switching (force-directed, hierarchical, circular, grid), search/highlight, node clustering, path highlighting. Support styling: map node metadata to size/color/shape, edge metadata to width/color/style. Include UI controls: filter panel (by metadata), layout selector, export screenshot (PNG/SVG), permalink for sharing. Optimize for graphs up to 1000 nodes (warn for larger graphs). Generate self-contained HTML with CDN-loaded libraries or optionally bundle dependencies.
tasks.rationale: Static graph exports (GraphML, DOT) require specialized software. Interactive web visualizations are shareable, accessible, and explorable without installing anything. Cytoscape.js is the leading web graph visualization library. This makes graphs instantly accessible to non-technical stakeholders and enables easy sharing/embedding.
acceptanceCriteria: Exports standalone HTML with embedded graph data
Interactive controls: pan, zoom, select, filter
Multiple layout algorithms available
Metadata mapped to visual properties
Search and highlight functionality
Screenshot export to PNG/SVG
Works for graphs up to 1000 nodes
Self-contained HTML requires no external files

tasks.title: Add performance optimization with caching and query planning
tasks.prompt: Implement comprehensive caching and query optimization layer in Store class. Add query_cache with LRU eviction for frequently-run queries (search, get_neighbors, get_subgraph), result_cache for expensive computations (centrality, clustering, embeddings), and metadata_index for fast filtering by metadata fields. Implement query planner that analyzes graph queries and chooses optimal execution strategy: indexed lookup vs. full scan, early filtering, join order optimization. Add cache warming on startup for common queries, cache invalidation on graph mutations, and cache statistics (hit rate, eviction count). Support configuration: cache_size_mb, cache_ttl_seconds, enable_query_planning. Include performance monitoring: query execution time, cache hit rates, index usage.
tasks.rationale: Performance becomes critical as graphs grow beyond 10k units. Naive graph traversal is O(n) or O(n²), but caching and indexing can reduce to O(1) or O(log n) for common operations. Query planning prevents pathological cases. These optimizations make the difference between unusable and production-ready for large graphs.
acceptanceCriteria: Query cache speeds up repeated searches by 10x+
Result cache eliminates redundant expensive computations
Metadata indexes enable fast filtering without full scans
Query planner chooses indexed lookup over full scan when beneficial
Cache automatically invalidates on graph mutations
Performance monitoring shows query times and cache hit rates
Configuration allows tuning cache size and TTL
Benchmarks show 5-10x improvement on typical workloads

executionPacks.name: search-features
executionPacks.description: Advanced search, browser extension, newsletter/sensor import, Cytoscape export, and performance optimization
executionPacks.rationale: These features enhance discoverability, data capture, and performance. All are independent and can be developed in parallel. Mix of store methods, imports, exports, and integrations provides variety while maintaining focus on search/discovery/performance theme.

executionPacks.name: versioning-collaboration
executionPacks.description: Graph versioning with history tracking and real-time collaboration with conflict resolution
executionPacks.rationale: Both features address multi-user scenarios and require sophisticated state management. Versioning is prerequisite for safe collaboration (users need rollback when collaboration conflicts can't auto-resolve). High technical complexity but clearly scoped. Can be developed sequentially: versioning first, then collaboration.
